name: Scrapper
tag: A laid-off line worker with a road sign and a grudge. Tough, close range.
good: standing in the middle of a fight. The most life in the game, armour skills, and swings that hit everything around you and can stun.
weak: anything that keeps its distance. Short reach and slow swings mean you chase ranged machines.
build: Wrecking Crew wades in and hits harder for each machine nearby. Immovable Object stacks armour and stuns the room with War Horn. Scrap Thrower throws scrap through the whole line, then rushes in to finish.

name: Technomancer
tag: An IT contractor who read the machines’ source and learned to curse in it. Fragile, ranged, clears crowds.
good: clearing crowds from a distance. Lightning that chains through a pack, stuns, and a turret and drones that fight for you.
weak: being caught. The least life in the game, hungry for energy, and you commit to one element (Schema).
build: Chain Reaction primes Arc Chain with Spark Lance and lets deadly strikes finish the pack. Sysadmin lets a turret, a Botnet and a storm do the fighting while you stay back. Control Rod stuns with Null Nova, slows with Packet Storm, and uses Step Back to get out.

name: Runner
tag: A courier who stopped delivering and kept running. Fast feet, faster hands.
good: moving and finding loot. The fastest class and the fastest attacks, dashes that nothing can touch, and the best credit and item finding.
weak: big single hits. Each blade hits light, and you avoid damage by not being there, not by armour.
build: Rush Hour throws a wall of blades, close and far, with a boomerang through the same line. Porch Pirate lures machines onto spike strips and blinks to where a marked one falls. Tip Jar plays for credits and gear, with kills by throw paying extra.

name: Anon
tag: No name, no face, no account. Traps, vanishing acts and a knife from behind.
good: one huge strike, and setting the fight up before it starts. Vanish and hit for nearly triple, a hop behind a machine that always lands a deadly strike, and mines and lures that pull machines where you want them.
weak: a long, open fight. Low life, and most of your damage needs setup time you may not get.
build: Demolition gathers machines with a Honeypot and blows them up with mines and Zip Bomb. Ghost banks charges with Rehearsal, hops in, vanishes, then spends the charges with The Dump. We Are Legion lets sockpuppets take the hits, then sets them all off and disappears.

name: Founder
tag: {He} left the Board with a grudge and a headcount. Summons a workforce and lets it do the dying.
good: letting other people fight. Interns, a drone and a hulking enforcer fight for you, each intern alive cuts the damage you take, and you can turn a machine to your side.
weak: being alone. Your own attacks are the weakest of any class, workers die and have to be hired again, and a bigger staff means you personally hit softer (Org Debt).
build: Headcount hires everyone and lets them grow stronger the longer they live. Hostile Takeover converts machines, then explodes your staff and the corpses. Iron Founder has no staff at all and fights in a Mech Suit.

name: Homesteader
tag: Lives on the verge the Office says does not exist. Tends a plot, wears a dead machine, or keeps a flock that does not love them.
good: owning a patch of ground. Rust plots slow and wear machines down, you can climb inside a tough machine shell, and you keep a flock of drones and a bull. The second-most life in the game.
weak: doing everything at once. Wearing a form ends your plots and switches off your flock, damage builds slowly, and drones that stray too far will bite you.
build: Cold Bed plants rust plots, feeds them with Compost and walls machines in with Hedgerow. Inside the Hull wears a machine shell whose armour grows the longer you stay in it. What Follows sends strays and a bull, then turns them into plots.

name: Witness
tag: Kept notes when Unity told everyone to stop looking. Stillwater watches and does nothing. The Witness writes it down. The record is paper.
good: one marked machine at a time. Watch a machine to build Testimony, then spend your Record on a single very large hit. Strong built-in damage reduction, and skills that make the whole party hit harder.
weak: crowds, and an empty Record. The slowest attacks in the game, no good way to clear a room, and the hardest class to learn.
build: The Page watches, delays the next blow, and pulls the thread for one big hit. Named in the Notes plays support, marking machines so allies hit harder. Above Eighty keeps the Record full for defence, with one save from death.

# that is the joke and also the build.

name: The Maximalist
tag: A paladin, essentially. {He} has not had a new thought since 2017 and has never needed one. {His} auras are always on, and everything {he} does is Sound damage, which nothing in this world resists.
good: never being resisted. Everything {he} does is Sound damage, which nothing resists. Always-on auras help everyone fighting beside {him}, and {he} gets stronger with more machines on screen.
weak: distance. {He} has to be close, and only one aura can be on at a time.
build: Orange Pilled keeps Marked to Market on, fires Cite Your Sources through it, and turns all other damage into Sound.
